I'm checking which color wins at intersections between vertical and horizontal bars across examples, but the results seem inconsistent — sometimes vertical wins, sometimes horizontal, so I need another rule to explain it.

I try width, area, and thickness comparisons, but each hypothesis breaks on some example, so I consider whether it's about drawing order or which bar was placed unbroken first.

Actually checking the input grids directly, whichever color already occupies the intersection in the input gets swapped to the opposite color in the output — the rule is simply to invert who's on top at every crossing point, and this holds consistently across all training pairs.
Understood — the rule is to swap which stripe is drawn on top at each crossing. Please provide the test input grid.
